L0·N8092unmasked layer
This neuron fires on word-internal/mid-phrase continuation pieces — subword fragments completing a longer word or compound (e.g. "poser" in "js-composer", "appointed" in "dis|appointed") and content words embedded mid-noun-phrase (" Calgary", " banquet", " Petite", " brainstorm") — while being maximally *suppressed* on capitalized words in the first position right after a newline ("experience", "Attempt", "Dummy", "COMP"), i.e. it tracks non-initial-in-line token position rather than any semantic topic.

This neuron is essentially a negatively-signed "quote" detector: it is strongly suppressed by the nouns "quote"/"quotation" (especially when introducing an attributed saying), while its weak positive/near-zero activations occur on other words that set up a citation or manner of speech ("as **the** great … observed", "in a **tone**", "in **formal** business writing", "**song**/word", author names like O'**Connor**).

L7·N2287unmasked layer
This is a weak, poorly-selective neuron that fires on clause/sentence-boundary punctuation tokens — closing quotes, commas in dates/lists, and periods (often ".\n" or "..\n") — with the same punctuation types (notably "?\n" after questions and heading-colons) producing its strongest negative values, so it appears to track punctuation-boundary position rather than any semantic content.

score 0.32punctuation token `,` following function calls or numerical parameters, typically in programming

score 0.32a token followed by a comma or semicolon

L12·N5798unmasked layer
Fires on generic, low-information continuation tokens right after a named entity or noun phrase — function words ("for", "and", "from"), list commas, and bland head nouns ("company", "place") — and is strongly suppressed on specific concrete/proper names in the same slot (brands, ingredients, technical terms like "basil", "oil", "DMC", "moderato").

This neuron's positive side fires weakly and diffusely on ordinary mid-sentence function/pronoun tokens (" it", " you", " isn", " New") and on odd acronym/name sub-word fragments ("BV" in RLBV, "ish" in Grisham), while it is most strongly *suppressed* on tokens that continue a multi-token proper name, company name, or chemical name (" Ltd", " Paul" in "Peter and Paul", "ash"/"ua" in Yahuashua, "-al" in "methylpropanal") — i.e. it mainly encodes "not part of an ongoing named-entity string."

L22·N11069unmasked layer
Fires on the token immediately preceding a numeral — usually the bare space (or a preposition/verb like "for"/"posted") right before a numeric quantity, especially counts and statistics (points scored, receptions/yards, stitch counts, class years); it is strongly suppressed at the analogous slot when the following number begins a calendar date ("on Jan. 20", " 9th March").
